sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US solar equipment makers are re-rating on falling financing costs and a stabilizing module price floor, which restores margin visibility for 2025 guidance.
Indonesia's renewables push is policy-led but execution-dependent, with biomass (TOBA) and EV/bus (VKTR) names benefiting from local-content mandates and captive demand, not global competitiveness.
The sector's durable driver is grid-scale storage and hybrid PPAs, which decouple revenue from volatile power prices and open new financing pools for developers like RUN and VST.
sectors.ai: Buy selective US solar equipment/developers (FSLR, SEDG, ARRY) on the post-election rate-cut repricing and module oversupply bottoming; Indonesia names (TOBA, VKTR) are momentum trades, not core holdings—take profits into strength. Watch for a pullback to add, as the sector's beta to rates remains high and Q4 earnings will separate real demand from subsidy noise.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's middle-class expansion and rising disposable income continue to drive premiumization in food, beverages, and personal care, benefiting agile mid-caps over bulky conglomerates.
Digital distribution and social-commerce penetration are structurally lowering customer-acquisition costs for FMCG players, enabling smaller brands to scale faster and disrupt incumbents.
Persistent rupiah volatility and imported-input inflation favor local-sourcing champions with pricing power, creating durable margin advantages for domestically integrated producers.
sectors.ai: Buy selective mid-cap consumer names with proven earnings delivery, not the broad index. ENZO, PADA, and MBTO show momentum but chase risk is high; favor AGAR and UDNG for relative value. Trim exposure to laggards, hold core staples for defensive carry, and add on any 3-5% pullback in quality franchises.
